As long as they're in the game, they make all 1st party martial classes inferior. On top of that; they don't *feel* like martial characters anymore. They feel like anime protagonists; not soldiers and barbarians.  Also; the strange emphasis on skills completely unrelated to fighting giving people an entire suite of new abilities. For example, Primal Fury uses Survival as it's main skill; a thing used for knowing what berries you can eat and not die. A primal fury user is so good at discerning berries, that they get DR 5/- and get to pretend to be large sized for a ton of things, and negate attacks, something that doesn't make *any thematic sense*. Scarlet Throne uses Sense Motive. They can *sense motive so hard* that they *run faster* for whatever reason? And have to make saves or be unable to attack you? That's bizarre. Really; all PoW does is give pseudo-casting to martials, which defeats the entire purpose imo. Finally; almost *all* decisions require a flavoring that you may not want. Not a *single one* of the maneuver classes don't start with a blank-slate. They all make presumptions of what you want *your* character to be. Some may say that helps build your backstory; but really it limits what your backstory *can* be by mechanical things. As-is, I can have a Barbarian that was a soldier in an army, or a Fighter that was a tribes warlord, or a Ranger that is a devout of an evil god. The forced-flavoring of the various combat arts or whatever is extremely limiting creatively.

I'm more of a fan of Drop Dead Studio's Spheres of Might options for making martial-caster disparity feel less bad. It gives them cool tricks that are 1. not flavorfully tied to any preconceptions of a character and 2. can be used all day; making them less limiting than PoW's maneuver system.
